title: New Metrics Endpoint Unreachable From Prometheus
intro: node-exporter was installed on web01, listening on 9100. Prometheus shows the target as DOWN with 'context deadline exceeded'.

steps.prompt: From the Prometheus server, test the port on web01 with a 5 second limit.
steps.fake_output: nc: connect to web01 port 9100 (tcp) timed out: Operation now in progress

steps.prompt: A timeout points at something dropping packets. On web01, confirm node-exporter is actually listening on all interfaces.
steps.hint: Rule out the service side before blaming the network.

steps.prompt: The service is fine. Check web01's host firewall.
steps.fake_output:
Status: active

To          Action   From
22/tcp      ALLOW    Anywhere
80,443/tcp  ALLOW    Anywhere

steps.prompt: 9100 isn't allowed, so the default policy drops it. Allow it only from the Prometheus server (10.0.9.5).
expected_commands: sudo ufw allow from 10.0.9.5 to any port 9100
ufw allow from 10.0.9.5 to any port 9100
sudo ufw allow from 10.0.9.5 to any port 9100 proto tcp
steps.hint: Scope the rule to the one source that needs it.

resolution: A classic timeout: the service was healthy and listening, but web01's host firewall had a default-deny inbound policy and nobody added a rule for the new port, so packets were silently dropped. Prometheus's 'context deadline exceeded' is just its way of saying 'timed out'. The refused-vs-timeout distinction pointed straight at network controls, and checking the service side first ruled out the app. In a cloud environment, remember there are often TWO layers to check — the host firewall (ufw/iptables) AND the cloud security group — and a timeout can come from either. Adding new ports to firewall rules should be part of the same change that deploys the new service, ideally in the same Terraform/Ansible code.
